title: $10k at 25 vs $10k at 35 — the gap is brutal
disclaimer: Hypothetical: one-time $10,000 at a 7% average annual return, compounded monthly. Not financial advice — real returns vary.

scenes.narration: Same ten thousand dollars. Same investment. One ends up with double the other. The only difference is ten years.
Invest ten thousand dollars one time, and leave it alone until sixty-five, at seven percent. One person does it at twenty-five, the other at thirty-five. Neither adds another cent.
One ten thousand dollar deposit, just ten years earlier. How big is the gap by sixty-five?

lines.text: How big is the gap at 65?

scenes.narration: At sixty-five, the twenty-five year old's ten thousand grew to about one hundred and sixty-three thousand. The thirty-five year old? About eighty-one thousand.
Same ten grand, same fund. Ten extra years roughly doubled it. Time is the real investor.
